observations.source: Controller of Budget, County Governments Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2024/25, section 3.38 (Siaya)
observations.note: The report states: the county generated KSh 436.68 million from its revenue sources, including health facility financing (FIF), and that this was 47 per cent of the annual target. It says this is 2 per cent more than KSh 427.95 million in FY 2023/24, but the FY 2023/24 report gave KSh 610.74 million for that year (see the trend). Press reports give the same 436.68 figure. The report also says the own-source revenue included KSh 290 million of arrears; how that splits the total is not clear from the text.

observations.source: Siaya County Secretary statement, as reported by K24 Digital
observations.note: Other statements say the county raised over KSh 900 million. The county's own document has not been read, so what it counts is unknown. The figure is close to the annual target implied by the Controller of Budget report (about KSh 929 million), which may explain it, but that is not established.

previous_year.source: Controller of Budget, County Governments Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2024/25, section 3.38 (Siaya)
previous_year.note: This comparator conflicts with the FY 2023/24 report, which gave KSh 610.74 million for FY 2023/24.

trend.caveat: Each year comes from a Controller of Budget report, and the reports count revenue differently and do not always agree. The FY 2023/24 report gives KSh 610.74 million for FY 2023/24, but the FY 2024/25 report gives KSh 427.95 million for the same year. FY 2022/23 is own-source revenue (KSh 402.23 million) plus appropriations-in-aid (KSh 105.81 million). Compare years with care.

points.source: Controller of Budget, County Governments Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2022/23, section on Siaya
points.note: Quoted in the FY 2022/23 report as the previous year's figure. Read from OCR text.

points.source: Controller of Budget, County Governments Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2022/23, section on Siaya
points.note: Own-source revenue KSh 402.23 million plus appropriations-in-aid KSh 105.81 million. The report says this was 17 per cent more than FY 2021/22.

points.source: Controller of Budget, County Governments Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2023/24, section 3.38 (Siaya)
points.note: As stated in its own year's report: the county generated KSh 610.74 million including health facility financing (FIF). Parts given: health FIF KSh 388.53 million and ordinary own-source revenue KSh 222.10 million, which add to 610.63 million. The report does not explain the 0.11 million difference.

alternate.source: Controller of Budget, County Governments Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2024/25, section 3.38 (Siaya)
alternate.note: The next year's report quotes KSh 427.95 million for FY 2023/24 and calls FY 2024/25 an increase of 2 per cent on it. Neither report explains the difference of about KSh 183 million.

points.corroboration: Search results also cite KSh 610.7 million for FY 2023/24 against a KSh 760 million target (80.4 per cent), attributed to the Controller of Budget table (Dawan Africa) and to the county's own plan for FY 2025/26. Neither source was read directly: the county plan link returned a not-found page. The KSh 427.95 million figure appears only in the FY 2024/25 report and a Nation article repeating it.

points.source: Controller of Budget, County Governments Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2024/25, section 3.38 (Siaya)

target.source: Controller of Budget, County Governments Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2024/25, section 3.38 (Siaya)
target.description: Own-source revenue counted in the approved budget financing: about KSh 1.04 billion, made up of KSh 643 million to be deposited into the County Revenue Fund and KSh 400 million as Appropriations-in-Aid spent at source.
target.note: The report says Siaya collected 47 per cent of its annual target. 436.68 divided by 0.47 gives about KSh 929 million, which is lower than the KSh 1,043 million in the budget financing. The report does not explain the difference.

budget.source: Controller of Budget, County Governments Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2024/25, section 3.38 (Siaya)
budget.note: Figures read from the scanned PDF with two OCR engines. They agree except the recurrent budget: the first read 6.02, the second read 6.07. 6.07 is used because 4.87 plus 6.07 equals the approved total of 10.94. The report states that recurrent spending was 83 per cent of the annual recurrent budget; 4.99 of 6.07 is 82.2 per cent, so the report may use a revised budget. The shares shown are the report's own statements. Check exact values in the printed tables.

pending_bills.note: The county reported KSh 1.12 billion pending at 30 June 2024 and settled KSh 577.7 million during FY 2024/25. The closing balance at 30 June 2025 could not be read reliably from the OCR text and is not shown.

stalled_projects.note: The county reported nine stalled development projects as of 30 June 2025. The project list in the PDF could not be read reliably, so individual projects are not shown.
